page: Amazon Web Services m9g.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 architecture using the Neoverse-V3 model, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with single-threaded execution per core. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and memory subsystem performance. The server achieves top-tier status in PassMark memory tests, PassMark database operations, and static web serving throughput. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also register in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Redis SET operations are rated as strong. However, single-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth fall into the average category. For machine learning workloads, the Neoverse-V3 processor delivers average prompt processing speeds for small and medium models, but exhibits weak text generation speeds for small models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides high resource density and strong multi-threaded performance per unit of compute resource, making it a viable option for scale-out workloads. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy storage-bound databases or deep learning training. Instead, the instance is suited for memory-intensive database operations, static web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and general-purpose application hosting where balanced CPU-to-memory ratios are required.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.8xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose instance powered by a 3.3 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores, 128.0 GB of memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps, running on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, the m9g.8xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in PassMark memory scores, database operations, and static web serving throughput, alongside strong multi-core CPU and Redis SET performance. However, single-core CPU performance is average, and text generation speeds for small language models are weak. Given its balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core and high-performing memory subsystem, this instance is suited for database operations, web serving, and multi-threaded processing workloads.
